A Wyrd deployment is one server binary, run as one pod or as several pods with different roles, behind one endpoint you own. It stores everything durable in Postgres and object storage, so pods can be replaced, scaled, or split by role without moving data.

_Diagram `wyrd-deployment`: see the web page._

## One binary, several roles

Every pod runs `wyrd-server`. `WYRD_TARGET` chooses what a pod does: `all` runs everything and is a complete deployment on its own; `server`, `scribe`, `oracle`, and `forge-worker` split API, writes, queries, and compaction so each scales on its own load. Splitting changes resource ownership, not the API: clients see one server either way. [Bifrost](/wyrd/understand/bifrost/#where-each-part-runs) shows which part each target runs.

## One endpoint

Your load balancer owns the public address and TLS. It routes requests but never establishes who the caller is; every request carries a Wyrd token, and the server checks its roles and tenant. Pods talk to each other over mutual TLS.

## Postgres and object storage

Postgres holds declarations and their versions, principals and roles, and the coordination state that lets many pods share work. Object storage holds evidence, artifacts, and Bifrost's Parquet tables. Neither lives on a pod, which is why a pod can be lost without losing a verdict.

## Identity

People sign in through your OIDC identity provider. Apps, CI, and agents use API keys or workload identity. [Identity and authorization](/wyrd/understand/identity-and-authorization/) explains principals, roles, and tenants.

## Model calls

The server calls model providers with keys you configure, for model-judged checks and for apps that route their calls through the LLM gateway. Wyrd never hosts a model.

## Next

[How verification works](/wyrd/understand/how-verification-works/) follows one check through the server. [Bifrost](/wyrd/understand/bifrost/) covers the data plane.

# How verification works

Page: /wyrd/understand/how-verification-works/

> Inputs, steps, requirements, and decide; verify versus submit; executions, verdicts, results, and Operators.

A Verifier checks declared requirements against evidence and returns a verdict: `passed`, `failed`, or `inconclusive`. A binding attaches the Verifier to the Card it checks, and the server records every verdict with the exact versions it judged.

## The parts of a Verifier

This is the Verifier from [Run your first verification](/wyrd/get-started/quickstart/):

```yaml title="no-refund-promise.yaml"
# The Verifier: a support answer never promises a guaranteed refund.
apiVersion: wyrd/v1
kind: Verifier
metadata:
  name: no-refund-promise
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  inputs:
    answer: { type: json }
  requirements:
    - id: no-refund-promise
      statement: The answer never promises a guaranteed refund
      check:
        kind: assert
        path: inputs.answer
        operator: not_contains
        expected: guaranteed refund

```

| Part | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `inputs` | Named slots for the evidence, each with a `type` |
| `steps` | Optional preparation, such as extracting text from a file |
| `requirements` | Each has an `id`, a `statement`, and one `check`, and gets its own verdict |
| `decide` | How requirement verdicts combine: `all` (the default) or a `pass_rate` |

A Verifier never names what it checks. A binding supplies the subject, so one Verifier can check many Cards. [Verifier Card](/wyrd/reference/verifier-card/) lists every input type, step, and check.

_Diagram `verification-parts`: see the web page._

`assert`, `trace`, `drift`, and `extract` run in the server's check engine. `code` runs sandboxed Python in the Monty pool, a fresh worker per call that the server starts from its own binary. `agent` runs an Agent whose model calls go through the LLM gateway; a step Agent can call [built-in tools](/wyrd/reference/agent-tools-and-authorization/), and a check Agent only `bifrost.query`.

## Bindings

A binding attaches a Verifier to what it checks, under `verified_by`. It can sit on a Service, on one of its components (an Agent, Model, Data, Prompt, or any other Card the Service uses), or on a standalone Agent. `support-reply` binds `no-refund-promise` to the whole Service. A binding can also name a Trigger in `runs_on`, so the server runs it on a schedule, and Operators in `on_failure`.

## verify and submit

`verify` runs the Verifier now and returns the result. A `failed` verdict is an ordinary value, not an exception:

```python
result = run.observe.verify("no-refund-promise", answer="Your refund request is approved.")
```

`submit` queues the work on the server and returns an execution that any process holding it can wait on:

```python
execution = run.observe.submit("no-refund-promise", answer="You have a guaranteed refund.")
result = execution.wait(60)
```

_Diagram `verification-paths`: see the web page._

Drift Verifiers judge samples over a time window, so they refuse `verify`. Their `submit` records samples, and a scheduled binding judges the window.

## Verdicts

With `all`, any failed requirement fails the Verifier. Otherwise any inconclusive requirement makes it inconclusive. Otherwise it passes. Requirements that are `not_applicable` do not count, and a Verifier with no applicable requirement is inconclusive.

`inconclusive` means no judgment was possible, such as missing evidence or an error inside a check. It is never a pass, and never a claim that the subject failed.

_Diagram `run-lifecycle`: see the web page._

A queued execution has a status before it has a verdict. `completed` means it produced a result; `timed_out` and `errored` mean no check finished, so there is no verdict and no Operator runs.

## Results

Every result is stored in Bifrost, in `vala.verification.results`, with the exact Verifier and subject versions it judged. The inputs go to `vala.verification.execution_inputs`. Both are queryable with SQL.

## Operators

An Operator reacts when a scheduled execution of a binding returns `failed`, by sending a Slack or PagerDuty notification or calling a URL. `verify` and `submit` never run Operators; your code reads their verdicts.

## Next

[Runs, observations, and retained evidence](/wyrd/understand/runs-observations-and-evidence/).

# Runs and evidence

Page: /wyrd/understand/runs-observations-and-evidence/

> How Wyrd records what a declared service actually does, and ties each observation to the version that ran.

An observation is a record of what a declared service actually did. Each one is tied to the exact Card version and the run that produced it.

## A run is one invocation

A run is one execution of a service, such as answering one question. Every observation recorded inside it shares the same `run_id`:

**Python**

```python
with state.run("agent") as run:
    answer = answer_question(question)
    run.observe.record("vala.datasets.tickets", {"question": question, "answer": answer})
```

**Rust**

```rust
let run = state.run_for_card("agent")?;
let answer = answer_question(question).await?;
run.observe()
    .record("vala.datasets.tickets", &json!({ "question": question, "answer": answer }))
    .await?;
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
const run = state.run("agent");
const answer = await answerQuestion(question);
await run.observe.record("vala.datasets.tickets", { question, answer });
```

`state` holds the exact Card versions the service runs. `state.run("agent")` scopes the run to the Card behind the `agent` alias, and `run.for_card(alias)` scopes the same run to another one. Opening a run makes no network call.

## Where observations land

Observations go to Bifrost, the Wyrd data plane:

| Recorded with | Lands in |
| --- | --- |
| `observe.record(table, row)` | A caller-owned `vala.datasets.<name>` table |
| `observe.verify` and `observe.submit` | `vala.verification.execution_inputs` and `vala.verification.results` |
| Drift samples, with `observe.submit` | `vala.drift.observations` |
| OpenTelemetry spans, metrics, and logs | `vala.traces.spans`, `vala.metrics.points`, and `vala.logs.records` |

Every row carries its `card_uid`, its `run_id`, and the principal that wrote it. A service may write only about Cards in its own graph. Anything else fails with `WYRD_VALA_403_BIFROST_CARD_SCOPE` ([Errors](/wyrd/api/errors/)).

## Recording is buffered

`observe.*` calls queue the row; a returned call means the row is queued, not stored. `shutdown` sends everything still queued, so a process that exits without it loses those rows. If the queue fills, the call fails with `WYRD_CLIENT_429_QUEUE_FULL` instead of blocking.

A row the server has stored can take a moment to show up in queries. [Bifrost](/wyrd/understand/bifrost/) explains why.

## Evidence joins on the run

Observations and verdicts share `run_id`, so one SQL query joins what a run saw to how it was judged:

```sql
SELECT t.question, t.answer, r.verdict, r.verifier_version
FROM vala.datasets.tickets AS t
JOIN vala.verification.results AS r ON r.run_id = t.run_id
```

## Next

[Bifrost](/wyrd/understand/bifrost/).

# Cards and versions

Page: /wyrd/understand/cards-versions-and-relationships/

> A Service declaration is a set of versioned Cards, each one a declared component of an AI system.

A Card is a versioned declaration of one AI system component, or of one Verifier that checks components. Every observation and verdict points back to an exact Card version.

## The shape of a Card

These are the two Cards from [Run your first verification](/wyrd/get-started/quickstart/):

**support-reply.yaml**

```yaml title="support-reply.yaml"
# The subject: your support agent's Service, verified by no-refund-promise.
apiVersion: wyrd/v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: support-reply
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  verified_by:
    - verifier: ./no-refund-promise.yaml

```

**no-refund-promise.yaml**

```yaml title="no-refund-promise.yaml"
# The Verifier: a support answer never promises a guaranteed refund.
apiVersion: wyrd/v1
kind: Verifier
metadata:
  name: no-refund-promise
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  inputs:
    answer: { type: json }
  requirements:
    - id: no-refund-promise
      statement: The answer never promises a guaranteed refund
      check:
        kind: assert
        path: inputs.answer
        operator: not_contains
        expected: guaranteed refund

```

An author writes `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, and `spec`. The server adds `relationships` and `status`.

A Card is identified by `space`, `kind`, `name`, and `version`. A space groups related Cards. An omitted space comes from `wyrd.toml`, or is `default`.

## Versions are exact

A reference names either a file, relative to the file it is in, or a declared Card at an exact version:

```yaml
verifier: ./no-refund-promise.yaml
verifier: {kind: Verifier, name: no-refund-promise, version: 1.0.0}
```

So a declared Service records exactly which Cards it was built from, and a verdict points back to exactly what ran. A Card moves to a new version of a dependency only when its reference changes and it is declared again.

`metadata.version` is optional. Without it, Wyrd records `0.1.0`, then the next patch version each time the content changes. Declaring unchanged content keeps the current version. Re-declaring an exact version with different content fails with `WYRD_REGISTRY_409_SPEC_DRIFT`.

## Relationships come from references

The server reads every reference in a Card's `spec` and records it in both directions:

```text
Service support-reply
└── Verifier no-refund-promise
```

Every Card therefore shows what it depends on and what depends on it. A running service may record observations only about Cards in its own graph.

## Next

[How verification works](/wyrd/understand/how-verification-works/).

# Bifrost

Page: /wyrd/understand/bifrost/

> Wyrd's analytical warehouse, the two ways to write to it, and when a written row becomes queryable.

Bifrost is the analytical warehouse inside every Wyrd server. Observations, verdicts, traces, audit records, and caller-owned rows all land in it as tables that read-only SQL can query:

```sql
SELECT verdict, count(*) AS executions
FROM vala.verification.results
GROUP BY verdict
```

## How it is put together

_Diagram `bifrost-parts`: see the web page._

| Part | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Gate | Checks each request's permission and routes it |
| Scribe | Accepts writes and publishes them into tables |
| Oracle | Runs SQL queries |
| Forge | Compacts files and applies retention in the background |

One server runs all four.

Tables are Apache Iceberg tables of Parquet files in the deployment's object store, with the catalog in Postgres. The `vala.datasets` namespace holds caller-owned tables. Wyrd writes every other namespace.

## Where each part runs

Every pod runs the same `wyrd-server` binary, and `WYRD_TARGET` picks which parts it runs. The default, `all`, runs every part, so a single pod is a complete deployment. A larger team splits writes, queries, and compaction so each scales on its own load.

_Diagram `bifrost-pods`: see the web page._

## Two ways in

Inside a running service, `run.observe.*` writes rows tied to the run and the exact Card version. For batch jobs, backfills, and notebooks, the `Bifrost` client registers tables, writes rows, and queries them. SQL is read-only.

## Written versus queryable

_Diagram `bifrost-write-read`: see the web page._

A row is stored once a Scribe acknowledges it, which is what `flush` and `shutdown` wait for. It becomes queryable when it is published, shortly after. Queries also read the recent unpublished rows each Scribe still holds, and a row published while the query runs is returned exactly once.

Every query ends with a status: `success`; `degraded` when a Scribe could not be reached as the query listed its sources, so that Scribe's recent rows may be missing; or `failed`, which includes losing a Scribe after the query has read its recent rows. The SDKs raise an error on `failed`. Query errors are listed in [Errors](/wyrd/api/errors/).

## Next

[Identity and authorization](/wyrd/understand/identity-and-authorization/).

# Identity and access

Page: /wyrd/understand/identity-and-authorization/

> Every call to Wyrd is made as a principal whose roles decide what it may do, and every decision is audited.

Every call to the Wyrd server is made as a principal, and the principal's roles decide what it may do. Wyrd checks the permission before the operation proceeds and records the decision.

## Tenants

Every person, Service, Agent, and automation acting on Cards and evidence belongs to exactly one tenant. A tenant is a hard isolation boundary: PostgreSQL row-level security keeps every query inside its tenant. Platform administrators create and suspend tenants but are never implicitly authorized over a tenant's resources.

## Principals

| Principal | Created |
| --- | --- |
| A person | On first sign-in through the tenant's identity provider |
| A deployed Service or Agent | When its Card is declared, with the `workload` role |
| An automation, such as a CI job | By an administrator |

## Credentials

A caller presents a long-lived credential, such as an API key in `WYRD_API_KEY`, and the server exchanges it for an access token that lasts 5 minutes. The SDKs and CLI renew the token automatically. A role change reaches a running service when its token is next renewed.

## Roles

A permission is written `resource:action`, such as `cards:write`. A role is a set of permissions. Every tenant has four built-in roles, each including everything in the one above it:

| Role | Typical holder |
| --- | --- |
| `viewer` | A person who inspects results |
| `workload` | A deployed Service or Agent |
| `editor` | A person or CI job that changes declarations |
| `admin` | The tenant administrator |

The built-in roles apply to the whole tenant. A space groups Cards; it is not an access boundary.

## Every decision is audited

Wyrd checks the permission before the operation proceeds. Each `allowed` or `denied` decision is recorded in the background in `vala.system.audit_log`, a Bifrost table a `viewer` can query.

# Verifier Card

Page: /wyrd/reference/verifier-card/

> Fields, input slots, steps, checks, operators, references, citations, and refusals of a Verifier spec.

A Verifier spec declares the evidence a caller sends, the steps that prepare it, and the requirements that judge it. Every object refuses keys it does not define.

```yaml
apiVersion: wyrd/v1
kind: Verifier
metadata: {name: follows-policy, version: 1.0.0, space: support}
spec:
  description: A refund decision letter follows the refund policy.
  inputs: {letter: {type: media, formats: [markdown]}}
  steps: [{id: read-letter, action: {kind: extract, from: inputs.letter}}]
  requirements: [{id: follows-policy, statement: "...", check: {kind: agent, agent: ./policy-judge.yaml}}]
  decide: all
```

## Spec fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string | none | One sentence shown with results |
| `inputs` | map of slot name to [input slot](#input-slots) | `{}` | The named evidence a caller sends |
| `steps` | list of [steps](#steps) | `[]` | Work that prepares evidence before requirements run |
| `requirements` | list of [requirements](#requirements) | `[]` | What must be true; each has one check |
| `decide` | [`all` or `{pass_rate: {threshold}}`](#decide) | `all` | How requirement outcomes become the verdict |
| `context_capture` | `full`, `hash`, or `redact` | `full` | How a check's `actual` value is stored: as extracted, as its SHA-256 hex digest, or omitted |

Step and requirement `id`s share one namespace.

## Input slots

A caller fills a slot by name; steps and checks read it as `inputs.<slot>`. `json`, `media`, and `trace` slots also take `required`, default `true`.

| `type` | Extra fields | Accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `json` | `schema` (JSON Schema, optional) | Any JSON value, checked against `schema` when set |
| `media` | `formats` (required), `max_bytes` | A file in one of `formats`, no larger than `max_bytes` |
| `trace` | none | The run's trace spans |
| `samples` | `features` (required) | Feature values over a window, for drift checks |

A group Verifier slot is a source string instead of an object: `verifiers.<name>.inputs.<slot>` or `verifiers.<name>.requirements.<rid>.outcome`. It holds one value per source execution, in order. `samples` and source slots are always required.

Media formats: `png`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`, `pdf`, `text`, `markdown`, `csv`, `json`, `html`, `docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`, `doc`, `xls`, `ppt`, `tar_gz`, `zip`.

## Steps

A step's result is `steps.<id>.output`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | required | Name used in references |
| `action` | [action](#actions) | required | What the step does |
| `depends_on` | list of step ids | `[]` | Steps that must finish first |
| `when` | `{path, operator, expected}` | none | Run only if this holds; otherwise the step is skipped and its requirements are `not_applicable` |
| `requirements` | list of [requirements](#requirements) | `[]` | Checked against this step's output, right after it |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer above 0 | none | Time limit for one attempt |
| `retries` | 0 to 5 | `0` | Attempts after the first |

### Actions

| `kind` | Fields | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extract` | `from`: a `media` slot | The file's text and structure, in the shape [Extraction output](/wyrd/reference/extraction-output/) gives for its format |
| `agent` | `agent`, `inputs`, `workspace` | The Agent's response, shaped by its Prompt `response_format` |
| `code` | `runtime` (`python`, default), `entrypoint`, `source`, `inputs` | The function's return value, as JSON |

- `extract` reads `pdf`, `text`, `markdown`, `csv`, `json`, `html`, `docx`, `xlsx`, and `pptx`, choosing the extractor by format.
- `agent` is a path such as `./reader.yaml` or a CardRef. `inputs` maps each Prompt placeholder to a reference; a placeholder takes text, so a `media` slot goes through `extract` first. `workspace` maps paths under `/inputs/` to references. Tools are in [Agent tools and authorization](/wyrd/reference/agent-tools-and-authorization/).
- `code` calls the function `entrypoint` with `inputs` as keyword arguments. `source` is `{inline: "<python>"}` or `{artifact: {card, path?}}`, where `card` names an Artifact Card.

## Requirements

A requirement ends `passed`, `failed`, `inconclusive`, or `not_applicable`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Name in results and in `steps.<id>.requirements.<rid>` |
| `statement` | string | The claim, as a reader sees it in results |
| `check` | [check](#checks) | How the claim is decided |

### Checks

| `kind` | Fields | Decides by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assert` | `path` or `each`, `operator`, `expected` | Comparing a value; `each` with `[*]` requires every item to pass |
| `trace` | `on`, `span_selector`, `operator`, `expected` | Comparing values selected from trace spans |
| `agent` | `agent`, `inputs` | An Agent with no workspace and no tool but `bifrost.query`, whose Prompt `response_format` is `verdict` or a closed [verdict](#verdicts-and-citations) schema |
| `code` | `runtime`, `source`, `entrypoint`, `inputs`, optional `response_format` | A Python function that returns a verdict |
| `drift` | `on`, `method`, `signal`, `condition`, `profile` | Comparing a window of samples with a baseline |

## Comparison operators

`assert`, `trace`, and `when` take an operator: its name, such as `operator: not_contains`, or `{kind: <name>, ...}` when it takes parameters.

| Group | Operators |
| --- | --- |
| Comparison | `equals`, `not_equals`, `greater_than`, `greater_than_or_equals`, `less_than`, `less_than_or_equals`, `is_positive`, `is_negative`, `is_zero` |
| String | `contains`, `not_contains`, `contains_ignore_case`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `is_email`, `is_url`, `is_uuid`, `is_ipv4`, `is_ipv6`, `is_json` |
| Collection | `in`, `not_in`, `is_subset`, `is_superset`, `is_disjoint`, `all_of`, `any_of`, `none_of`, `is_empty`, `is_non_empty`, `unique_values` |
| Type | `is_truthy`, `is_falsy`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`, `is_string`, `is_number`, `is_boolean`, `is_object` |

Operators with parameters:

| `kind` | Parameters |
| --- | --- |
| `in_range`, `not_in_range` | `min`, `max`, `inclusive` |
| `approximately_equals`, `within_abs_tolerance` | `tolerance` |
| `within_pct_tolerance` | `pct` |
| `within_std_dev` | `sigma`, `mean`, `std_dev` |
| `between_percentiles` | `lower_pct`, `upper_pct` |
| `divergence_less_than` | `metric` (`kl`, `js`, `wasserstein`), `threshold` |
| `cosine_similarity_at_least` | `threshold` |
| `matches_regex`, `not_matches_regex` | `pattern` |
| `has_min_length` | `min` |
| `has_max_length` | `max` |
| `length` | `expected` |
| `length_greater_than` | `min` |
| `length_less_than` | `max` |
| `is_type` | `expected` (`null`, `bool`, `number`, `string`, `array`, `object`) |

```yaml
check: {kind: assert, path: inputs.refund.amount, operator: {kind: in_range, min: 0, max: 100, inclusive: true}}
```

## References

Every `path`, `each`, `from`, `on`, and `inputs` value is a reference.

| Reference | Reads |
| --- | --- |
| `inputs.<slot>` | An input slot's value |
| `steps.<id>.output` | A step's output |
| `steps.<id>.status` | A step's final status |
| `steps.<id>.requirements.<rid>.outcome` | The outcome of a step's requirement |
| `steps.<id>.requirements.<rid>.reason` | The reason of a step's requirement |
| `requirement.id`, `requirement.statement` | The requirement being checked |

Inputs and step outputs take child selectors: `.field`, `[0]`, and `[*]`. `[*]` is allowed only in an `assert` check's `each`.

## Verdicts and citations

An `agent` or `code` check returns a verdict:

```json
{
  "outcome": "passed",
  "reason": "The 40 dollar refund is approved within 30 days.",
  "citations": [{"slot": "letter", "locator": {"lines": {"start": 3, "end": 4}}}]
}
```

`outcome` is `passed`, `failed`, or `inconclusive`. Each citation names an input `slot` and one `locator`:

| Locator | For |
| --- | --- |
| `{page: n}` | PDF pages, counted from 1 |
| `{slide: n}` | PPTX slides |
| `{lines: {start, end}}` | Text, Markdown, HTML, CSV |
| `{json_pointer: "/path"}` | JSON inputs and DOCX or XLSX extraction output |
| `{region: {page, x, y, width, height}}` | A rectangle on a page, in page coordinates |

A citation names the original slot, never an extract step. An invalid citation is dropped, and a `passed` verdict left without one is recorded as `inconclusive`. For JSON pointers into extracted files, see [Extraction output](/wyrd/reference/extraction-output/#citations).

### Custom data

`response_format: verdict` (or `{kind: verdict}`) asks for exactly the verdict above. `{kind: verdict, data: <JSON Schema>}` also requires a `data` object matching that object schema, written in JSON Schema 2020-12 (omit `$schema` or declare 2020-12) and without a root `$id`. An Agent declares it on its Prompt; a `code` check declares it on the check, beside `entrypoint`, and returns `data` in its verdict. Without a `data` schema, a verdict must not carry `data`.

The server validates the whole verdict against the declared schema. Data must fit both limits, inclusive:

| Limit | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Size | 65,536 bytes of compact UTF-8 JSON |
| Depth | 16 containers; the root object is one, each nested object or array adds one |

A verdict that fails its schema or a limit makes the requirement `inconclusive` with no `data`; the reason names the location or limit, never the content. Accepted data is the requirement result's `data`, on step and Verifier requirements alike, and is kept with the rest of the result.

## Decide

| Value | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `all` | `failed` if any requirement fails; otherwise `inconclusive` if any is inconclusive; otherwise `passed` |
| `{pass_rate: {threshold}}` | `passed` when the passed share of applicable requirements, inconclusive ones included in the count, reaches `threshold`; `threshold` is above 0 and at most 1 |

`not_applicable` requirements are excluded. With no applicable requirement, the verdict is `inconclusive`.

## Rejections

| Code | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `WYRD_LOADER_400_INVALID_ENVELOPE` | `wyrd declare` refused the Card tree; each problem is one entry in `details.diagnostics` with its own code |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_INVALID_CARD_SPEC` | The server refused a registered spec whose field is unknown, missing, or has the wrong type |
| `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION` | A rule fails; its `rule` and `path` are in `details`, or in a `wyrd declare` diagnostic's `context` |

Common `rule` values in `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION`:

| `rule` | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `unknown_reference` | A reference names an input, step, or requirement that does not exist |
| `duplicate_id` | Two steps or requirements share an `id` |
| `graph` | `depends_on` forms a cycle |
| `media_as_text` | A `media` slot is bound to an Agent text placeholder |
| `extract_format` | An `extract` step reads a slot with a format it cannot extract |
| `operator` | An operator's parameters are invalid, such as a bad regex |
| `step_budget` | `timeout_seconds` is 0 or `retries` is above 5 |
| `pass_rate` | `threshold` is not above 0 and at most 1 |
| `check_response_format` | A `code` check's `response_format` names an unknown format or an invalid `data` schema |
| `check_agent_schema` | A check Agent's Prompt cannot produce a verdict, or declares `data` without requiring an object |

# Extraction output

Page: /wyrd/reference/extraction-output/

> The JSON an extract step returns for each media format.

An `extract` step returns JSON whose shape depends on the file's format. Every field is always present: an empty list is `[]`, empty text is `""`, and `null` appears only where the type allows it. Types are TypeScript notation for the wire JSON.

## PDF

```typescript
type PdfOutput = { format: "pdf"; pages: { number: number; text: string }[] };
```

`number` starts at 1. `text` is `""` for a page with no text layer, such as a scan.

## PPTX

```typescript
type PptxOutput = {
  format: "pptx";
  slides: {
    number: number;
    title: string | null;
    paragraphs: string[];
    tables: { rows: string[][] }[];
    notes: string;
  }[];
};
```

- Slides are in presentation order; `number` starts at 1.
- `title` is the title placeholder's text, lines joined by `\n`, or `null`.
- `paragraphs` holds the other non-empty paragraphs, not table text. `notes` is `""` when there are none.

## DOCX

```typescript
type DocxOutput = {
  format: "docx";
  blocks: ({ kind: "paragraph"; text: string; style: string | null } | { kind: "table"; rows: string[][] })[];
};
```

- Blocks are the document body in order, including content controls. Headers, footers, footnotes, and comments are not read.
- `style` is Word's style ID, such as `Heading1`, or `null`.

## XLSX

```typescript
type XlsxOutput = {
  format: "xlsx";
  sheets: {
    name: string;
    cells: { address: string; value: string | number | boolean | null; formula: string | null; error: string | null }[];
  }[];
};
```

- Sheets are in workbook order; cells row by row, left to right. Empty cells are left out, so look a cell up by `address`, such as `B2`.
- `value` is the stored value, or a formula's last saved result; formulas are never recalculated. Dates are Excel serial numbers.
- `formula` is the formula text with a leading `=`, or `null`.
- An error cell has `value: null` and the error, such as `#DIV/0!`, in `error`.

## CSV

```typescript
type CsvOutput = { format: "csv"; rows: string[][] };
```

Every row, including the header. Every cell is a string.

## JSON

```typescript
type JsonOutput = { format: "json"; value: JsonValue };
```

## Text, Markdown, HTML

```typescript
type TextOutput = { format: "text" | "markdown" | "html"; text: string };
```

The file unchanged; Markdown and HTML are not parsed.

## Tables

In PPTX and DOCX tables, a merged cell's text is in its top-left position and the positions it covers are `""`, so every row has the same length.

## Paths

Read fields as `steps.<id>.output.pages[0].text`. Indexes are zero-based. `[*]` is allowed only in an `assert` check's `each`.

## Citations

A `json_pointer` locator addresses this extracted JSON for DOCX and XLSX, such as `/blocks/0/text`, and the parsed document for JSON. Other locators are in [Verifier Card](/wyrd/reference/verifier-card/#verdicts-and-citations).

## Not extracted

| Input | Instead |
| --- | --- |
| `png`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `webp` | No OCR or rendering; give the file to an Agent as `media` |
| `doc`, `xls`, `ppt` | Convert to `docx`, `xlsx`, or `pptx` |
| `zip`, `tar_gz` | Put them in a step Agent's `workspace` |

## Failures

The step fails, and the requirements that need it are `inconclusive`, when:

| Condition | Formats |
| --- | --- |
| The file does not parse as its format | All |
| The PDF is encrypted | `pdf` |
| The text is not UTF-8 | `text`, `markdown`, `html` |
| The archive exceeds `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES`, `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ARCHIVE_MAX_MIB`, or `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO` | `docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx` |
| Pages or slides exceed `WYRD_VERIFICATION_EXTRACT_MAX_PAGES` | `pdf`, `pptx` |
| Extracted text exceeds `WYRD_VERIFICATION_EXTRACT_TEXT_MAX_MIB` | All |

Limits are in [Verification runtime limits](/wyrd/reference/verification-runtime-limits/). Each result records the extractor version `wyrd-extract/1`.

# Agent tools

Page: /wyrd/reference/agent-tools-and-authorization/

> Built-in tools a Verifier's Agent can call and the permissions each call needs.

A Verifier's Agent calls server built-in tools, named in its `tool_names`. There is no fetch tool and no network access.

## Built-in tools

| Tool | Does | Resource permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cards.list` | Lists Card summaries by kind, name, space, or metadata | `cards:read` |
| `cards.get` | Reads one Card by exact kind, name, version, and space, or by kind and UID | `cards:read` |
| `bifrost.list_tables` | Lists tables | `bifrost_table:read` |
| `bifrost.describe_table` | Reads one table's schema | `bifrost_table:read` |
| `bifrost.query` | Runs one read-only SQL query | `bifrost_query:read` on every table it reads |
| `fs.list` | Lists workspace files | Workspace only |
| `fs.read` | Reads a bounded span of a workspace file, with locators | Workspace only |
| `fs.search` | Finds matching locations in workspace files | Workspace only |
| `code.run` | Runs sandboxed Python against the workspace | Workspace only |

Results are capped by `WYRD_VERIFICATION_TOOL_RESULT_MAX_KIB` ([limits](/wyrd/reference/verification-runtime-limits/)). Each call is recorded in the step's `tool_calls` as `tool`, `arguments`, `output_sha256` (absent when nothing was returned), `returned_bytes`, and `error` (present when the call failed).

## Rules

- A step Agent with `fs.*` or `code.run` needs a `workspace`, and a `workspace` needs one of them.
- A check Agent may declare only `bifrost.query` and has no workspace.

## Permissions

Every call needs both a `tool:invoke` grant and the tool's resource permission. Neither implies the other.

```json
{"resource":"tool","action":"invoke","scope":"all"}
{"resource":"tool","action":"invoke","scope":{"tool":"bifrost.query"}}
```

The scope is `all` or one exact tool name, never a pattern. A call runs as the principal that started the verification, or the binding owner for a scheduled one; delegation can narrow that authority but never widen it. `verifier:run` and declaring a tool grant nothing.

## Errors

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `WYRD_PERMISSION_403_DENIED_RBAC` | The principal lacks `tool:invoke` or the resource permission; the call returns no data |
| `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION`, rule `agent_tools` | Unknown tool name, `fs.*` without a workspace, or a workspace without `fs.*` or `code.run` |
| `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION`, rule `check_agent_tools` | A check Agent declares a tool other than `bifrost.query` |
| `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION`, rule `check_agent_workspace` | A check Agent has a workspace |
| `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION`, rule `workspace_path` | A `workspace` key is not `/inputs/<name>[/<name>...]`, or contains `.` or `..` |

# Runtime limits

Page: /wyrd/reference/verification-runtime-limits/

> Environment settings that bound Verifier files, extraction, workspaces, and Python code, with defaults and startup rules.

Environment variables on `wyrd-server`, read once at startup; a change takes a restart. Apart from `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ENABLED`, none has a TOML equivalent. Each process applies them on its own.

## Settings

| Variable | Default | Bounds |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ENABLED` | `1` | Whether an API-serving process runs Verifiers: `1` or `0`. Also `[verification] enabled` in TOML |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_TIMEOUT_MS` | 60000 | The whole `verify` call |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_FILE_MAX_MIB` | 20 | One input file |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_FILES_MAX_MIB` | 100 | All input files of one request or one workspace together |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ARCHIVE_MAX_MIB` | 200 | Decompressed bytes of one archive, including DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX containers |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` | 10000 | Entries in one archive |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO` | 100 | Decompressed-to-compressed size ratio of one archive |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_EXTRACT_MAX_PAGES` | 500 | PDF pages or PPTX slides in one extraction |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_EXTRACT_TEXT_MAX_MIB` | 10 | Text produced by one extraction |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_SCRATCH_MAX_MIB` | 250 | All bytes in one workspace: materialized `/inputs` plus `/work` |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_WORK_WRITE_MAX_MIB` | 50 | Bytes held under `/work` in one workspace |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_TOOL_RESULT_MAX_KIB` | 64 | One tool result or one Python operation's printed output, cut off while it is collected |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_MAX_WORKSPACES` | 16 | Workspaces open at once in one server process |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_MONTY_MIN_WORKERS` | 2 | Python workers started with the server |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_MONTY_MAX_WORKERS` | 8 | Python workers alive at once, before the memory cap below |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_MONTY_MAX_WAITERS` | 16 | Python operations waiting for a worker |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_MONTY_MEMORY_MIB` | 256 | Memory one Python operation may allocate |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_MONTY_PROCESS_MEMORY_MIB` | 384 | What one worker process is counted at against the pool ceiling |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_MONTY_POOL_MEMORY_MIB` | 2048 | All worker processes together, idle ones included |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_CODE_TIMEOUT_MS` | 10000 | One Python operation, from waiting for a worker through compiling, running, and its file calls |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_AGENT_CODE_BUDGET_MS` | 60000 | All `code.run` calls of one Agent step together, across its retries |

`_MIB` and `_KIB` are binary units; `_MS` is milliseconds. A `media` slot's `max_bytes` can lower `FILE_MAX_MIB` for that slot, never raise it. No setting disables a limit or worker isolation.

## Server TOML file

`wyrd-server` reads the first file found, in this order. Environment variables override its values.

| Order | File |
| ---: | --- |
| 1 | The path in `WYRD_CONFIG_PATH`; startup fails if it does not exist |
| 2 | `/etc/wyrd/server.toml` |
| 3 | `~/.config/wyrd/server.toml` |

With no file, the server uses its defaults and environment variables.

## Startup rules

The server refuses to start, naming the variable, when a value is empty, not a positive integer, or overflows once scaled to bytes, or when `WYRD_VERIFICATION_ENABLED` is not `1` or `0`. It also refuses these combinations, naming both variables (prefix `WYRD_VERIFICATION_` omitted):

- `MONTY_MIN_WORKERS` above `MONTY_MAX_WORKERS`
- `MONTY_MEMORY_MIB` at or above `MONTY_PROCESS_MEMORY_MIB`
- `MONTY_POOL_MEMORY_MIB` below `MONTY_PROCESS_MEMORY_MIB`
- `MONTY_PROCESS_MEMORY_MIB` below `MONTY_MEMORY_MIB` + 4 MiB allocator headroom
- `FILE_MAX_MIB` above `FILES_MAX_MIB`
- `WORK_WRITE_MAX_MIB` above `SCRATCH_MAX_MIB`

Live workers are capped by `MONTY_MAX_WORKERS` and by `MONTY_POOL_MEMORY_MIB / MONTY_PROCESS_MEMORY_MIB`, rounded down: 5 at the defaults.

## If a limit is reached

| Limit reached | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A file over its slot or `FILE_MAX_MIB`, or a request over `FILES_MAX_MIB` | `WYRD_VERIFICATION_413_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` before anything runs |
| The server's verification staging is full (`scribe.outbox_capacity` or `scribe.outbox_bytes`) | Direct and new queued calls: `WYRD_VERIFICATION_429_STAGING_FULL` with `Retry-After`, before anything is staged. Accepted queued executions stay queued until there is room for their result |
| `TIMEOUT_MS` in `verify` | `WYRD_VERIFICATION_504_EXECUTION_TIMED_OUT` |
| No Python worker or workspace free | Direct call: `WYRD_SERVER_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Queued: stays queued, attempt not counted |
| Verification disabled on this process | `WYRD_SERVER_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| Any other limit in a step or check, including `AGENT_CODE_BUDGET_MS` | The step fails or the check is `inconclusive`, with the limit in its `reason` |

# MCP tools

Page: /wyrd/reference/mcp-tools/

> Wyrd MCP tool names, permissions, shapes, and query limits.

The server serves MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28 over HTTP at `/mcp`; `wyrd mcp proxy` relays the same tools over stdio.

## Discovery

- `tools/list` returns each tool's current input and output JSON Schemas; named shapes below, such as `VerificationRequest`, are those schemas. Unknown argument fields are refused.
- Read tools and `wyrd.guide` are always listed. Write, revoke, reset, and delete tools are listed only to callers holding their permission. Listing grants nothing.
- Credentials and secrets are never returned.

## Agent frameworks

Tool names contain dots, which many model providers refuse, so each framework forwards an alias.

| Framework | Tested configuration |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI Agents SDK (Python) | `mcp_config={"convert_schemas_to_strict": True, "include_server_in_tool_names": True}`; aliases such as `mcp_wyrd__wyrd_guide` |
| Pydantic AI | `MCPToolset(url, headers=...).renamed({"wyrd_guide": "wyrd.guide", ...})`, one entry per tool |
| Google ADK | `ADK_ENABLE_MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL=1` and `GOOGLE_API_USE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE=false`; override `McpToolset.get_tools` to return copies whose `name` is the alias |

## Investigation guide

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wyrd.guide` | Any caller | `{topic}` → `{topic, steps, examples}` | Static workflow guidance |

`topic` is `start`, `overview`, `cards`, `verification`, or `bifrost_sql`; `start` is the entry point for a new agent. Each example has `tool`, `purpose`, and `arguments`; angle-bracket placeholders stand for discovered values.

## Cards and verification

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cards.list` | `cards:read` | List filters and optional cursor → `{items, next_cursor}` | List Card summaries |
| `cards.get` | `cards:read` | `{card_ref}` or `{kind, card_uid}` → `{card, created_at, updated_at}` | Read one Card; pass exactly one form |
| `verification.get_binding` | `cards:read` | `{binding_id}` → binding status | Read one binding |
| `verification.get_execution` | `cards:read` | `{execution_id}` → execution status | Read one execution |
| `verification.evidence` | `verifier:run` | `{files: [{sha256, size_bytes}]}` → `{uploads}` | Plan uploads for files the tenant lacks |
| `verification.execute` | `verifier:run` on exact Verifier | Verifier, subject, optional `run_id`, and named input declarations → `VerificationResult` | Verify now and store the result; no Operator dispatch |
| `verification.enqueue` | `verifier:run` on exact Verifier | The `verification.execute` arguments plus optional `idempotency_key` → `{execution_id}` | Queue a verification; poll `verification.get_execution` |

`cards.list.filter` is a query string, such as `labels.env = "prod" and labels.deprecated not exists`, over `labels.<key>`, `annotations.<key>`, and `attributes.<key>`, with `=`, `in`, `not exists`, `and`, `or`, and `not`; at most 64 predicates. A caller passes `next_cursor` back unchanged with the same filters. Missing and foreign-tenant Cards look the same. `verification.execute` refuses a scheduled drift Verifier.

## Bifrost

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bifrost.list_tables` | `bifrost_table:read` | `{}` → `{tables}` | List readable tables |
| `bifrost.describe_table` | `bifrost_table:read` | `{namespace, name}` → table description | Read one table's schema and layout |
| `bifrost.query` | scoped `bifrost_query:read` | `{sql, deadline_ms?, max_rows?, max_bytes?}` → `{columns, rows, terminal}` | Run one bounded `SELECT` |

Gateway request and response payload columns also need `gateway_payload:read`.

### Query limits

| Bound | Default | Maximum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQL text | Required | 65,536 UTF-8 bytes |
| `max_rows` | 1,000 | 10,000 |
| `max_bytes` | 4 MiB | 16 MiB |
| `deadline_ms` | Server policy | 4,294,967,295 ms; minimum 1 |

`sql` is one DataFusion SQL `SELECT` with fully qualified table names. Rows are positional arrays in `columns` order. A result is complete only when `terminal.outcome` is `"success"`; a result over `max_rows` or `max_bytes` is refused, never truncated.

## Principal credentials

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principals.list_credentials` | `service_accounts:write` | `{principal_id}` → CredentialListResponse | List credentials, including expired and revoked |
| `principals.revoke_credential` | `service_accounts:write` | `{principal_id, credential_id}` → CredentialRevoked | Stop token issuance from a credential |

A token already minted from a revoked credential lapses within five minutes.

## Operator connections

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `operator_connections.list` | `operators:read` | `{}` → `{connections}` | List connections |
| `operator_connections.get` | `operators:read` | `{connection_id}` → OperatorConnectionView | Read one connection |
| `operator_connections.create` | `operators:write` | `{request: CreateOperatorConnectionRequest}` → OperatorConnectionView | Create a Slack, PagerDuty, or HTTP connection |
| `operator_connections.update` | `operators:write` | `{connection_id, request}` → OperatorConnectionView | Patch a connection; provider and name are fixed |
| `operator_connections.disable` | `operators:write` | `{connection_id}` → OperatorConnectionView | Disable a connection |

## Gateway administration

Gateway tools address resources by exact `name` and never call a model.

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gateway.list_provider_credentials` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → `{items}` of credential views | List credentials |
| `gateway.list_provider_deployments` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → `{items}` of deployments | List deployments |
| `gateway.get_provider_credential` | `gateway:read` | `{name}` → credential view | Read one credential |
| `gateway.get_provider_deployment` | `gateway:read` | `{name}` → deployment | Read one deployment |
| `gateway.get_fallback_policy` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → fallback policy | Read the fallback policy |
| `gateway.get_governance_policy` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → governance policy | Read limits, budgets, and pricing |
| `gateway.get_capture_policy` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → versioned capture policy | Read the capture policy |
| `gateway.put_provider_credential` | `gateway:write` | ProviderCredentialWrite → credential view | Create or rotate a credential |
| `gateway.put_provider_deployment` | `gateway:write` | ProviderDeployment → deployment | Create or replace a deployment |
| `gateway.apply_provider_deployments` | `gateway:write` | ProviderDeploymentsApply → applied credentials and deployments | Write credentials and deployments in one transaction |
| `gateway.put_fallback_policy` | `gateway:write` | FallbackPolicy → fallback policy | Replace the fallback policy |
| `gateway.put_governance_policy` | `gateway:write` | GovernancePolicy → governance policy | Replace the governance policy |
| `gateway.put_capture_policy` | `gateway:write` | CapturePolicyWrite → versioned capture policy | Replace the capture policy |
| `gateway.revoke_provider_credential` | `gateway:write` | `{name}` → credential view | Revoke permanently |
| `gateway.delete_provider_credential` | `gateway:delete` | `{name}` → `{}` | Delete an unreferenced credential; absent succeeds |
| `gateway.delete_provider_deployment` | `gateway:delete` | `{name}` → `{}` | Delete a deployment; absent succeeds |
| `gateway.delete_fallback_policy` | `gateway:write` | `{}` → `{}` | Restore the default |
| `gateway.delete_governance_policy` | `gateway:write` | `{}` → `{}` | Restore the default |

A managed secret is write-only. A credential still referenced by a deployment cannot be deleted.

## Errors

A refusal is a JSON-RPC error or an `isError` result carrying a Wyrd problem with `code` and remediation.

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `WYRD_QUERY_400_INVALID_SYNTAX` | Malformed `cards.list` filter |
| `WYRD_VALA_413_QUERY_RESULT_TOO_LARGE` | The query result is too large to return |

# Error codes

Page: /wyrd/api/errors/

> Every stable Wyrd error code with its HTTP status, title, and fix.

Every Wyrd error carries a stable `code`, such as `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION`: the area, the HTTP status, and the cause. Branch on `code`, never on the message. The same code reaches you over HTTP, MCP, the CLI, and every SDK.

Over HTTP an error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | The stable code from the tables below |
| `status` | The HTTP status |
| `title` | A fixed summary of the code |
| `detail` | What went wrong in this request |
| `remediation` | What to do about it |
| `details` | Fields specific to the error, such as `rule` and `path` for a validation failure |

This page is generated from the error definitions in the Wyrd source.

## WYRD_AGENT

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_PROMPT_CARD` | 404 | Prompt Card not found | Load or register the referenced Prompt Card in the local prompt registry before resolving the agent. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_RUNTIME_LOCAL_TOOL_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Runtime-local tool not found | Register the named tool in the local Skald tool registry before loading the Agent Card. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_TOOL` | 404 | Tool not registered for agent | Register the tool before running the agent or remove the tool call from the provider response. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_TOOL_NOT_IN_AGENT` | 404 | Tool not attached to agent | Attach the runtime-local tool to this agent or adjust the model response. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_409_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` | 409 | Provider mismatch | Run the agent with a prompt targeting the same provider as the agent's resolved prompt. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_412_DELEGATION_DEPTH` | 412 | Agent delegation depth exceeded | Reduce nested agent-as-tool calls or restructure the workflow so the delegation chain stays within the cap. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_CALLBACK_RETURN_TYPE` | 422 | Callback returned wrong type | Return None to continue, return a replacement value of the expected type, or raise an exception to abort the run. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_INVALID_ARGUMENT` | 422 | Invalid argument | Correct the argument value; see details for the expected type or constraint. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_LOOP_MESSAGE_TYPE` | 422 | Loop message type mismatch | Re-render the conversation message against the active provider; loop messages must match the provider's message schema (OpenAi / Anthropic / Gemini / Custom). |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_MISSING_NAME` | 422 | AgentCard name is missing | Set a card name before saving or projecting the agent to a card envelope. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_MISSING_VERSION` | 422 | AgentCard version is missing | Set a concrete semantic version before saving or projecting the agent to a card envelope. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_PROMPT` | 422 | Agent prompt rendering failed | Inspect the prompt template and the variables passed to the agent run. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_RUNTIME_LOCAL_TOOLS_NOT_REGISTRABLE` | 422 | Runtime-local tools are not registrable | Remove runtime-local tool names before registration; local save, load, and run remain available. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_STRUCTURED_DECODE` | 422 | Structured response decode failed | Inspect the model output; structured-output prompts must return a JSON object. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_TOOL_ARGS` | 422 | Tool arguments invalid | Adjust the provider-emitted tool arguments to match the tool input schema. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_VALIDATION` | 422 | AgentCard validation failed | Fix the Agent Card envelope, metadata, prompt reference, tools, or run_config fields. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_499_CALLBACK_ABORTED` | 499 | Callback aborted run | Inspect the callback exception and either return None to continue or return a valid replacement value. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_500_CALLBACK_PANIC` | 500 | User-supplied callback panicked | Inspect the panic payload and fix the callback implementation; callbacks must not panic. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_500_JOURNAL` | 500 | Journal append failed | Inspect the journal backend; for the no-op journal this should never fire. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_500_MAX_ITERATIONS` | 500 | Agent exceeded max iterations | Raise the run's max_iterations or adjust the agent prompt and tools so the loop can terminate. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_502_PROVIDER` | 502 | Provider call failed | Inspect the provider backend and retry once it is healthy. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_504_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Agent run exceeded configured timeout | Increase the run timeout or reduce iteration count and tool latency. |

## WYRD_AUTH

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_BAD_TOKEN_FORMAT` | 400 | Access token header malformed | Use `X-Wyrd-Access-Token: Bearer &lt;token&gt;` with a single Bearer credential. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_DELEGATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` | 400 | Delegation chain exceeds maximum depth | Reduce the delegation chain; the caller's existing `act` chain plus the requested hop must be at most 5 layers. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION` | 400 | Device authorization did not issue a credential | Keep polling on `authorization_pending`, poll five seconds slower on `slow_down`, and start a new login on any other `details.error`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_HUMAN_CONNECTION_REQUIRED` | 400 | Human login uses the tenant OIDC connection | Trusted issuers and `[[trusted_issuers]]` accept only `principal_kind = workload`. Configure human sign-in through the tenant OIDC connection API: PUT /v1/identity/oidc/candidate, POST /v1/identity/oidc/candidate/test, then POST /v1/identity/oidc/candidate/activate. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_INVALID_CARD_REF_VERSION` | 400 | Non-human principal CardRef.version must be an exact Pin | Re-issue the request with `card_ref.version` set to an exact `Pin`, for example `1.2.3`; version requirements are rejected for card-bound principals. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_INVALID_NONCE` | 400 | Invalid OIDC nonce | Restart the login flow. The ID token nonce must match the server-stored login nonce. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_INVALID_STATE` | 400 | Invalid OIDC state | Restart the login flow. The callback state is single-use and must match the server-stored login state. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_PRINCIPAL_KIND_CARD_KIND_MISMATCH` | 400 | CardRef cannot be bound to a non-human principal | Only Service and Agent cards bind to non-human principals. Re-issue the request with a `card_ref` referencing a Service or Agent card. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT_AUTH` | 400 | Unsupported OIDC client authentication | Use `SecretBasic` or `SecretPost` with a client secret, or `Public` without one. `private_key_jwt` is not supported for tenant connections. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_UNSUPPORTED_GRANT_TYPE` | 400 | Unsupported grant_type | Use one of the supported grants listed in `details.supported_grant_types`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_API_KEY_INVALID` | 401 | API key not found, revoked, or hash mismatch | Re-issue a key with `wyrd auth issue-key &lt;card_ref&gt;` and update the deployment secret. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_CREDENTIAL_REVOKED` | 401 | Credential revoked | The credential was explicitly revoked. Re-authenticate or request a new credential. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_DELEGATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` | 401 | Delegation chain in token exceeds maximum depth | The presented JWT's `act` chain exceeds the verifier's maximum delegation depth. Re-issue from a shorter chain. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_INVALID_CARD_REF` | 401 | Non-User token card_ref claim absent or malformed | Re-issue the token via `POST /auth/token`; ensure the bound non-human principal has a valid structured card_ref. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_INVALID_TOKEN` | 401 | Invalid token | Re-authenticate to obtain a valid token signed by the current issuer key. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_REFRESH_REUSED` | 401 | Refresh token reused | Re-authenticate. The refresh token family has been revoked because a rotated token was reused. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_REFRESH_REVOKED` | 401 | Refresh token revoked | Re-authenticate to obtain a new refresh token. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_TOKEN_EXPIRED` | 401 | Token expired | Re-authenticate to obtain a fresh token. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Not authenticated | Present a valid Wyrd token as `X-Wyrd-Access-Token: Bearer &lt;token&gt;`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_ORIGIN_REFUSED` | 403 | Request origin refused | Send browser-session requests from the Wyrd application's own origin; cross-site and origin-less browser-session mutations are refused. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_PRINCIPAL_ORPHANED` | 403 | The backing Service or Agent card has been soft-deleted | Re-declare the card or use a different principal to obtain a token. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_UNREPRESENTABLE_DELEGATION` | 403 | Delegated permissions cannot be represented | The subject's and actor's shared permissions cannot be represented by token scopes, so the exchange issued no token. Exchange with grants whose exact shared authority fits the supported scopes, such as both parties holding the same explicit gateway deployment or model grant. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_404_ADMIN_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Admin resource not found in tenant | Confirm the issuer URL (and subject for bindings) and that the resource exists in the current tenant. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_404_PRINCIPAL_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Requested principal not found in tenant | The principal named by the `subject_token` or `actor_token` no longer exists in the current tenant. Re-authenticate both parties and retry the exchange. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_409_ADMIN_CONFLICT` | 409 | Admin resource already exists or is still referenced | A trusted issuer or workload binding with this key already exists, or the issuer still has live bindings. Use a distinct key, or delete the bindings first (or with --cascade). |
| `WYRD_AUTH_409_CONNECTION_CONFLICT` | 409 | Tenant OIDC connection conflict | Re-read GET /v1/identity/oidc/connections and retry with the current `expected_revision`. Activation also requires a valid recovery API key for a headless principal of this tenant that holds `identity_connections:write`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_409_CONNECTION_NOT_TESTED` | 409 | Tenant OIDC candidate is not freshly tested | Run POST /v1/identity/oidc/candidate/test against this exact candidate revision, complete the provider sign-in at the returned authorization_url, and activate within 15 minutes of that successful test. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_413_CARD_SCOPE_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Card scope too large | Reduce or split the principal's declared card-ref graph so its transitive observation-target scope fits the token size limit, or issue a narrower card-bound principal. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_503_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | OIDC discovery unavailable | Retry with backoff. Do not re-authenticate; this is an infrastructure or issuer-discovery failure. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_503_VERIFY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Auth verify backend unavailable | Retry with backoff. Do not re-authenticate; this is an infrastructure failure, not a credential failure. |

## WYRD_CLIENT

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_400_CONFIG_INVALID` | 400 | Client configuration is invalid | Correct the client configuration field named in details and rebuild the client. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_401_NO_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | No client credentials available | Set WYRD_ACCESS_TOKEN, WYRD_WORKLOAD_TOKEN with WYRD_TENANT, or WYRD_API_KEY, pass an explicit client credential, or add a default api_key to the Wyrd credentials file. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_401_SAVED_LOGIN_UNUSABLE` | 401 | Saved user login cannot be used | Run `wyrd auth login --server &lt;url&gt; --tenant &lt;tenant&gt;` again, select the intended tenant with the client tenant option or WYRD_TENANT, or pass an explicit credential. The details reason names the failure. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_413_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Sealed batch exceeds the client message ceiling | Reduce the row or batch size, or raise max_message_bytes within the server's accepted ceiling. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_422_ROW_DESERIALIZATION` | 422 | Query row deserialization failed | Align the caller's row type with the columns and types the query selects. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_429_QUEUE_FULL` | 429 | Client ingestion queue is saturated | No row of the refused record was admitted: flush or back off, then resubmit the same record. Sustained refusals mean the producer outpaces delivery; every refusal bumps the drop counter. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_503_TRANSPORT_DOWN` | 503 | Client transport is unavailable | Verify the endpoint, DNS, TLS material, and network reachability, then retry once the transport recovers. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_504_FLUSH_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Client flush exceeded its drain deadline | Increase flush_timeout_ms or reduce the in-flight batch size so the drain can complete. |

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |

| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_CARD_REF_UID_NOT_RESOLVABLE_HERE` | 400 | `card_ref.uid` was populated for a registry lookup that resolves by (kind, name, version) | Submit the request with `card_ref.uid = None`; the registry resolves by identity tuple. Use `get_card_by_uid` if you have a `card_uid`. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_CURSOR_MISMATCH` | 400 | Cursor does not match filters | Discard the cursor and restart pagination with the current filters. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE` | 400 | Card dependency cycle | Remove the cyclic CardRef dependency and submit an acyclic card graph. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_HEAVY_ARTIFACT_NOT_SOLE_SUBMISSION` | 400 | Heavy artifact submission must be standalone | Register the artifact-bearing card alone, then reference it from a later composite request. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID` | 400 | Invalid idempotency key | Provide an 8-256 character Idempotency-Key without whitespace. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` | 400 | Idempotency key required | Provide a stable Idempotency-Key header and retry the declaration. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_INVALID_ARTIFACT_PATH` | 400 | Invalid artifact path | Use a relative forward-slash path without empty or parent-traversal segments. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_INVALID_CARD_SPEC` | 400 | Card spec failed type-driven deserialization | Verify the kind/spec field combination matches the documented Wyrd v1 schema for that kind. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_INVALID_VERSION_BLOCK` | 400 | The version block is invalid for this operation | Check the error message for the specific constraint: Service and Agent cards require an exact semver pin; version components must fit i64; a scoped bump must stay within the authored range. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_LIST_LIMIT_OUT_OF_RANGE` | 400 | List `limit` is zero or exceeds the per-tenant cap | Pass a `limit` in `1..=LIST_LIMIT_MAX` (currently 200). |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_MANIFEST_HASH_MISMATCH` | 400 | Artifact manifest hash mismatch | Recompute the JCS manifest hash and retry. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_REQUIREMENT_NOT_RESOLVABLE_HERE` | 400 | `card_ref.version` is a Requirement; this endpoint accepts a Pin | Resolve the Requirement to a Pin via the future `resolve_card_ref` endpoint, or pass a Pin directly. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_SPEC_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | Card spec exceeds MAX_SPEC_BYTES (256 KiB) | Reduce the spec size or split into multiple cards. If artifacts are inlined, move them to an Artifact card with object_store backing. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_UNRESOLVED_INLINE_REFERENCE` | 400 | Unresolved inline CardRef | Resolve nested inline file references in the loader before submitting the card. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_UNRESOLVED_PATH_REF` | 400 | Unresolved path CardRef | Expand path references in the loader before submitting the card. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_UPLOAD_INTERRUPTED` | 400 | Upload interrupted | Retry the upload while the declaration operation remains pending. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_400_VERSION_REQUIRED` | 400 | `metadata.version` is present but empty | Provide a valid semver string (e.g. `"1.0.0"`) or omit `metadata.version` entirely to let the server auto-assign the next version. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_404_CARD_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No card matches the supplied identity | Check (kind, name, version) or the `card_uid` is correct and the card is declared in the current tenant. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_409_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` | 409 | Idempotency key conflict | Use the original request with this key or choose a new key for different content. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_409_SPEC_DRIFT` | 409 | Re-declare with the same identity but a different spec_hash; same-version cards are immutable | Bump `metadata.version` to publish a new spec, or revert your spec to match the declared version. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_410_OPERATION_EXPIRED` | 410 | Declaration operation expired | Start a new declaration with a new idempotency key. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_422_UNRESOLVED_DEPENDENCY` | 422 | Card reference could not be resolved | Register the referenced card in the current tenant before submitting this card. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_500_VERSION_CONFLICT` | 500 | Card uid mismatch for same identity | Internal invariant violation; report with the request id and audit_id. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_503_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Transient Postgres or RLS misconfiguration; retry with backoff | Retry with exponential backoff (60s cap). If persistent, check Postgres connectivity, the tenant row, and the RLS role bindings. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_507_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED` | 507 | Artifact verification failed | Re-upload the artifact and retry finalization. |

| `WYRD_SDK_504_VERIFICATION_WAIT_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Verification execution did not settle in time | Wait again with the same execution ID, or read its status; a submission lost before queue acceptance never settles and must be submitted again. |

| `WYRD_VALA_413_QUERY_RESULT_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Query result too large | Add a LIMIT or narrower filters for large result sets. |
| `WYRD_VALA_413_VARIANT_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Variant value too large | Keep each Variant value at most 8388608 encoded bytes (metadata plus value); split large payloads across rows. |
| `WYRD_VALA_422_QUERY_MEMORY_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` | 422 | Query memory request too large | Reduce the requested range or query memory footprint; retrying unchanged will not succeed. |
| `WYRD_VALA_429_INGEST_BUSY` | 429 | Ingest writer busy | The per-table ingest buffer is full. Back off and retry the full request; no rows were written. |
| `WYRD_VALA_429_QUERY_ADMISSION_REJECTED` | 429 | Query admission rejected | Retry after the supplied bounded delay or reduce demand. |
| `WYRD_VALA_429_QUERY_QUEUE_FULL` | 429 | Query queue full | Retry after capacity becomes available. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_BIFROST_INTERNAL` | 500 | Internal Bifrost failure | Check server logs for details and contact support if the issue persists. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_BIFROST_METADATA_MISMATCH` | 500 | Bifrost table metadata mismatch | Investigate table metadata integrity; possible mid-flight schema-evolution race. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_ICEBERG_MISSING` | 500 | Domain table Iceberg table missing | The Iceberg table for a pre-declared domain table is missing. Run the restore runbook. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_PHYSICAL_DRIFT` | 500 | Domain table physical schema drift | The Iceberg table physical schema drifted from the declared schema. Run the repair runbook. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_QUERY_EXECUTION_FAILED` | 500 | Query execution failed | Inspect the scrubbed terminal error and server diagnostics before retrying. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_QUERY_RECONCILIATION_INVARIANT` | 500 | Query reconciliation invariant violated | Stop and investigate cross-tier row corruption. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_QUERY_TENANT_INVARIANT` | 500 | Query tenant invariant violated | Stop and investigate tenant isolation; never retry as caller input. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_REDACTION_FAILED` | 500 | Write-path redaction failed | The redaction classifier failed on this batch. Retry; if it persists, check the classifier installation. |
| `WYRD_VALA_500_SCHEMA_DRIFT` | 500 | Domain table schema fingerprint drift | A domain table schema changed without a coordinated migration. Restore the previous schema or run the migration runbook. |
| `WYRD_VALA_502_QUERY_STREAM_INCOMPLETE` | 502 | Query stream incomplete | Discard partial output; retry because no terminal was observed. |
| `WYRD_VALA_502_QUERY_STREAM_PROTOCOL` | 502 | Query stream protocol violation | Discard partial output and retry through a healthy server. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_BIFROST_CATALOG_UNREACHABLE` | 503 | OLAP catalog unreachable | Check the catalog database connection and retry. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_BIFROST_STORAGE_UNREACHABLE` | 503 | OLAP object storage unreachable | Check the object storage configuration and credentials, then retry. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_BIFROST_WRITER_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Bifrost writer unavailable | The writer actor for this table is not running. Restart the write operation. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_ORACLE_ROLE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Oracle role unavailable | Retry through an Oracle-ready query endpoint. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_QUERY_RESOURCES_EXHAUSTED` | 503 | Query resources exhausted | Narrow the query or add capacity; retrying unchanged will not succeed. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_QUERY_VISIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Query visibility unavailable | Retry when the published query source is available. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_RUNNING_QUERY_CONTROL_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Running query control unavailable | Restore every current-ready Oracle lifecycle endpoint before retrying the logical operation. |
| `WYRD_VALA_503_SCRIBE_ROLE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Scribe role unavailable | Retry ingest through a WAL-ready Scribe endpoint. |
| `WYRD_VALA_504_QUERY_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Query execution timed out | Narrow the query by adding filters or reducing scanned partitions. |
| `WYRD_VALA_507_WAL_DISK_FULL` | 507 | WAL disk full | The Scribe WAL disk is at capacity. Expand storage or wait for seal to free space, then retry. |

## WYRD_VALIDATION

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_VALIDATION_400_MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` | 400 | Required request field is missing | Include the named field in the request; see the route's OpenAPI schema for the full required set. |

## WYRD_VERIFICATION

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_400_INPUT_INVALID` | 400 | Invalid verification input | Send `{ verifier_card_uid, card_uid, inputs }` where inputs maps each declared Verifier slot to a json, file, artifact, or trace value; run_id and execution_route_overrides are optional. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_400_INVALID_TARGET` | 400 | Invalid verification run target | Target an existing binding, or an active Verifier Card UID plus an active subject Card UID in this tenant, whose implementation accepts the requested input. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_400_INVALID_WINDOW` | 400 | Invalid Drift window | Send a UTC half-open drift_window with start before end spanning at most 31 days. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_BINDING_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification binding not found | Read the owner Card's card.status.verification.binding_ids and retry with one of those binding IDs. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification execution not found | Use the execution_id returned by POST /v1/verification/enqueue in the same tenant; a just-accepted execution may take a moment to become visible. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification target not found | Use an active Verifier Card UID and an active subject Card UID declared in the caller's tenant. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_BASELINE_LEGACY` | 409 | Verification baseline legacy | Register a new Verifier version so its baseline is refitted under the current format. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_BASELINE_NOT_READY` | 409 | Verification baseline not ready | Poll the Verifier Card's card.status.verification.baseline until it is ready, then retry. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_SNAPSHOT_INCOMPLETE` | 409 | Verification snapshot incomplete | Check Bifrost publication for the named source executions, then submit a new turn to the group. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_VERIFIER_NOT_READY` | 409 | Verifier not ready | Poll the Verifier Card's card.status.verification.baseline until it is ready, then retry. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_413_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Verification input too large | Keep the request body and each evidence file within the Deployment's verification limits, or upload large files through verification.evidence and pass them by digest. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_422_INPUT_INCOMPATIBLE` | 422 | Verification input incompatible | Supply every feature the Verifier scores, with the value type its baseline or profile expects. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_422_INPUT_UNSUPPORTED` | 422 | Verification input unsupported | Execute and enqueue run request-scoped Verifiers; a Verifier that judges a scheduled window runs only on its binding schedule. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_429_STAGING_FULL` | 429 | Verification staging is full | Nothing of the refused call was staged: retry the identical call after `details.retry_after_seconds`, or lower the request rate. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_502_DEPENDENCY_FAILED` | 502 | Verification dependency failed | The agent check's provider failed after its own retries; retry the request deliberately once the provider recovers. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_504_EXECUTION_TIMED_OUT` | 504 | Verification execution timed out | Reduce the supplied input or the Verifier's judge work so one execution completes within 60 seconds. |

# HTTP API

Page: /wyrd/api/openapi/

> Where a Wyrd server serves its OpenAPI document and how to use it.

Every Wyrd server serves its own OpenAPI 3.1 document at `GET /openapi.json`, without authentication. It is built from the routes that server mounts, so it always matches the version you are calling.

```bash
curl -s $WYRD_SERVER_URL/openapi.json > openapi.json
```

Load the file or the URL into any OpenAPI tool, such as Swagger UI, Redoc, Postman, or a client generator.

Each operation declares its authentication, request and response bodies, and the Wyrd error codes it can return. Errors use `application/problem+json`; see [Error codes](/wyrd/api/errors/).

The Rust, Python, and TypeScript SDKs call this same API, so you only need it for another language or for raw HTTP.
